title: Provable Authorization Orchestration and Retention Playbook
author: Aisha Khan
body:
Overview
-------
This playbook defines an operable, testable approach to producing provable authorization (authz) evidence for Redwood Inference across changes to RBAC, service identity, and cross-region deployments. The intent is to ensure that for any authorization decision or entitlement change we can: (a) reconstruct who changed what and when, (b) surface relevant audit traces for investigations, and (c) package verifiable evidence that meets compliance reviewers' expectations.

Scope and goals
----------------
- Scope: All control-plane and data-plane authorization events for hosted and dedicated deployments, evidence emitted by the API gateway, authorization service (authz), IAM syncs, and the audit pipeline.
- Goals:
  - Ensure complete capture of authorization events required for forensic reconstruction within 15 minutes of occurrence.
  - Provide a standard evidence bundle format that can be produced on-demand for audits and incident response.
  - Define retention tiers and automated shredding policies that map to legal/regulatory boundaries.
  - Integrate with incident response and compliance workflows for fast handoff.

Why this is necessary
---------------------
Redwood operates multi-tenant inference environments (hosted, dedicated, private). Authorization evidence needs to be:
- Tamper-evident (cryptographic linkage where possible)
- Region-aware (data residency constraints)
- Searchable/fast to export for regulatory and internal investigations

Key concepts and terminology
---------------------------
- Authorization event: Any change or evaluation that affects access (grant, revoke, decision, delegation, role assignment, role binding).
- Evidence bundle: A packaged set of artifacts (audit events, policy version, role definition, snapshot of membership, hashes) sufficient to re-create an authorization decision path.
- Snapshot ID: Deterministic identifier for a time-bound state of RBAC policy and membership (used to correlate events).

Architectural overview
----------------------
1) Sources of truth:
   - IAM catalog (identities, service accounts)
   - Policy store (OPA/PEP/compiled policies)
   - Role and entitlements DB (authoritative role definitions and bindings)
   - API gateway and authz service logs
2) Evidence flow:
   - Authz event -> enriched by evidence-collector (adds Snapshot ID, policy hash) -> audit-queue -> immutable audit store (WORM) -> evidence-orchestrator packages bundle on request
3) Owners:
   - Evidence-collector service: eng-sre (owner: eng-sre/runtime-observability)
   - Policy store: eng-platform (owner: eng-platform/policy-team)
   - Evidence orchestrator & export UI: security (owner: security/compliance-ops)

Evidence bundle format (text form)
--------------------------------
Each evidence bundle is a line-delimited JSON archive plus a manifest. Example manifest fields: 
- bundle_id, generated_at, tenant_id, snapshot_id, policy_hashes, included_event_ids, region, retention_profile, signer_key_id

Example manifest (single-line JSON):
{"bundle_id":"bndl-20260602-9f2a","generated_at":"2026-06-02T15:22:10Z","tenant_id":"tenant-123","snapshot_id":"snap-20260602-15","policy_hashes":["sha256:abcd..."],"included_event_ids":["evt-991","evt-992"],"region":"eu-west-1","retention_profile":"standard-7y","signer_key_id":"kms:projects/redwood/keys/evidence-prove"}

Retention profiles and mapping
----------------------------
| retention_profile | description | archival_ttl | access_ttl | shred_after | notes |
| standard-2y       | Default for non-sensitive operational authz events | 24 months | 90 days | 30 months | Applies to non-EU tenants unless contract specifies otherwise |
| standard-7y       | Default for enterprise contracts with extended audit needs | 84 months | 365 days | 90 months | Used for customers with SOC/ISO/FIN reporting requirements |
| legal-hold        | Indefinite until release by legal | indefinite | indefinite | upon release | Marked by legal hold ID and cannot be auto-shredded |

Automation rules
----------------
- On any role-binding change: evidence-collector must create a snapshot and emit an event containing snapshot_id and policy_hash.
- On policy compile: policy store publishes policy_hash and policy_version into the audit-queue.
- If an event references data in a restricted region, orchestrator enforces regional packaging and export controls.

Operational play steps (fast incident handoff)
---------------------------------------------
1. Triage (security oncall)
   - Identify tenant(s), timeframe, and impacted identities.
   - Mark incident in PagerDuty and attach preliminary labels (RBAC, Data Residency, Urgent).
2. Evidence request
   - Run: rwdctl evidence request --tenant tenant-123 --from 2026-06-01T00:00:00Z --to 2026-06-02T16:00:00Z --scope authz
   - Evidence-orchestrator returns bundle_id and estimated completion time (target <= 15 min for in-scope events).
3. Packaging and verification
   - Orchestrator packages manifest + line-delimited events + role snapshots + policy artifacts.
   - Orchestrator signs manifest with KMS-managed key and records signer_key_id in manifest.
4. Delivery
   - For internal investigations: encrypted bundle pushed to secure S3 (region limited) and a link shared on the incident ticket.
   - For legal/compliance: signed bundle exported to evidence custody with chain-of-custody record.

Example CLI usage
-----------------
# request evidence for a tenant, CLI prints bundle id
rwdctl evidence request --tenant tenant-123 --from 2026-06-01 --to 2026-06-02 --scope authz

# fetch the bundle and verify signature
rwdctl evidence fetch --bundle bndl-20260602-9f2a | jq -r .manifest > manifest.json
verify-signature --manifest manifest.json --kms-key-id kms:projects/redwood/keys/evidence-prove

Checks and SLOs
---------------
- Evidence emission SLO: 99% of role-binding events produce an evidence event within 15 minutes. Owner: eng-sre.
- Bundle generation SLO: 95% of on-demand evidence bundle requests complete within 15 minutes for windows up to 72 hours. Owner: security.
- Signature verification SLO: 99.9% of bundles can be verified using active KMS keys. Owner: eng-platform/security-infra.

Testing and validation
----------------------
- Monthly simulation run: eng-sre triggers synthetic RBAC changes for three tenants (hosted, dedicated, private) and validates end-to-end bundle generation and signature verification.
- Annual audit: compliance team runs a full retention and shredding simulation and verifies that legal holds block shredding.

Exception handling and risk table
--------------------------------
- Risk: Snapshot mismatch (events reference invalid snapshot_id)
  - Impact: Incomplete reconstruction, medium
  - Mitigation: Re-run collector in area of mismatch, use raw event stream + compiled policy versions to reconstruct, contact engineering to extract source DB snapshot.
- Risk: Evidence bucket region conflict
  - Impact: Regulatory exposure, high
  - Mitigation: Orchestrator enforces region-aware packaging; if mis-packaged, immediately trigger legal hold and replicate to correct regional store.

Change management (how to update this playbook)
------------------------------------------------
1. Proposed changes must be submitted as an ADR in confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records with a linked test plan.
2. Security & eng-sre review and sign-off required for changes to retention_profile or evidence bundle format.
3. After approval, run the monthly simulation and publish change notes on this page.

Owner and contacts
------------------
- Playbook owner: Aisha Khan (security/compliance-ops)
- Tech owner: Eng-SRE runtime-observability (oncall alias: eng-sre-runtime@redwood.example.com)
- Legal liaison: Priya Shah (legal@redwood.example.com)

Appendix A — evidence query recipes
----------------------------------
- Find role assignment events for user@example.com in a timeframe:
  jq -c 'select(.event_type=="role_binding") | select(.principal=="user@example.com")' /var/audit/stream/2026-06-01.ndjson.gz | head -n 50
- Correlate policy compile to decision ID:
  SELECT event_id, policy_version, decision_id FROM audit_events WHERE event_type='policy_compile' AND policy_hash='sha256:abcd...' LIMIT 100;

Appendix B — FAQ
----------------
Q: Who can request evidence bundles?
A: Authorized contacts: tenant admins, security oncall, legal, and the compliance review group. Requests from non-authorized accounts must be escalated.

Q: Can bundles be redacted?
A: Yes — orchestrator supports column and field redactions for exports that must be delivered to third parties. Redaction must be recorded in the manifest with the redaction_policy_id.

Related documents
-----------------
- Refer to the policy-store compile contract and event schema in the architecture docs.
